dish: Contemporary izakaya small plates and craft cocktails — rotating Japanese-American bites with an open kitchen bar
address: 948 W Erie Plaza Dr, Erie, PA 16505
w: Chefs Dan Kern (of 1201 Kitchen) and Adam Williams' contemporary Japanese izakaya in West Erie Plaza — Erie Reader's 2024 Best Restaurant and a near-winner for Best Sushi, prized as much for its craft cocktails as its food.

dish: Street tacos on fresh-made tortillas — asada, al pastor and chorizo topped simply with onion and cilantro; also birria tacos
w: A family-owned downtown taqueria in the old Modern Tool building since 2016, swept Erie Reader's Best Taco and Best Mexican honors in both 2024 and 2025 — the taco anchor of the city's evolving Mexican scene.

dish: Made-from-scratch traditional Italian pastas and red-sauce classics from a fourth-generation Erie family recipe
w: Amanda Serafini, great-granddaughter of the founder of the original 1938 Serafini's, revived the family name downtown and was named Erie Reader's Best New Restaurant of 2025 — scratch Italian rooted in Erie's deep Italian community.

dish: Belgian-style abbey ales — dubbels, tripels and quads — plus porters, from a monk-themed nano-brewery
w: A small west-side brewery on the Lake Erie Ale Trail devoted to Belgian styles (dubbels, tripels, quads) with 16-plus taps and rotating food trucks — a distinctive specialist among Erie's breweries.

dish: Hand-crafted espresso drinks and house-made soups, wraps and baked goods in a quirky neighborhood cafe
w: A woman-owned Little Italy-adjacent cafe that took Erie Reader's Best Coffee three years running (2021–23), beloved for community vibes and made-in-house food alongside its coffee.

dish: Coffee roasted in-house (the roastery is in the basement) — single-origin pour-overs, plus breakfast sandwiches
n: Brew Ha Ha at the Colony
w: One of the rare Erie coffee shops that roasts its own beans on site, near Colony Plaza on the west side — a repeat Erie Reader Best Coffee honoree pairing house-roasted coffee with a relaxed cafe menu.

dish: Locally-roasted single-origin coffee brewed to order — pour-over, Chemex or french press — and La Marzocco espresso
w: A community-minded downtown coffee bar (named for the building's chandlery past and Erie's manufacturing 'forge') serving locally-roasted single-origin coffee; a fixture of the State Street revival past its fifth year.

dish: Sponge candy cooked in aged copper kettles and hand-dipped, plus meltaways — Old-World Italian confection since 1929
w: An Erie chocolate institution founded in 1929 by Italian immigrant Romolo Stefanelli and now run by four sisters from Meadville, making small-batch sponge candy over copper kettles — the third pillar of Erie's sponge-candy trio with Romolo and Pulakos.

dish: Estate wines on Route 20 in Lake Erie Wine Country, with Meet-the-Winemaker and vineyard-picnic tours
address: 10021 W Main Rd, North East, PA 16428
w: A North East winery along Route 20 producing wines from local Lake Erie AVA vineyards, offering intimate guided tastings and seasonal picnic-in-the-vineyard experiences — a solid stop on the wine-belt drive beyond the big three.

dish: One of the region's largest selections of sweet, fruit, port and sparkling wines, with a Lake Erie-view deck
address: 12160 E Main Rd, North East, PA 16428
w: Run by the Bostwick family, whose Lake Erie grape-growing roots span generations, this longtime North East favorite is known for an enormous range of sweet and fruit wines and a scenic tasting deck overlooking the lake.

dish: Small-batch estate wines — from Gewürztraminer to the best-selling 'Derby Red' Concord/Fredonia blend — in a pre-Civil War barn
w: Harborcreek's first winery (2012), founded by two Penn State Behrend grads in a preserved 100-plus-year-old horse barn on the eastern edge of the wine belt, making small batches from local Lake Erie AVA fruit.
